chunks: From him, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Harun ibn Jariya who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I intermingle with the Magians, so I eat from their meals.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No'.

key_terms.الْمَجُوسِيَّ: The Magian (Zoroastrian), a specific People of the Book in Shia fiqh

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating the food of Magians in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Harun ibn Jariya seeks clarification from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding the permissibility of consuming food prepared by Magians (Zoroastrians), a specific group of *Ahl al-Kitab* with distinct theological views. The Imam’s concise response of 'No' (*La*) is interpreted by Shia jurists as a definitive prohibition (*haram*), distinguishing the ruling for Magians from that of Jews and Christians in certain schools of thought. This ruling underscores the importance of ritual purity and the specific status of Zoroastrians in Shia fiqh, particularly in contexts of social interaction and dietary laws.
